# operator-auth

<!-- Generated by tools/config-reference.py from libs/platform-pf/src/main/resources/META-INF/oidf-settings/operator-auth.json. Do not edit: change the catalogue, then run python3 tools/config-reference.py. -->

The settings of the `operator-auth` component of `libs/platform-pf`, read by package `com.pingidentity.ps.oidf.platform.pf.auth`: generated from its catalogue, operator-auth.json, by `tools/config-reference.py`, and checked in CI. [How to read a row](README.md#reading-a-row).

Families: `OIDF_OPERATOR_`. A name under one of these that no catalogue declares is an unknown key.

Under the production profile a violation by one of these settings refuses `OPERATOR_API` (components).

| Setting | Default | What it does | When it's wrong | Profile | Security |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OIDF_OPERATOR_AUTH_MODE` | `jwt`; one of `jwt`, `introspection` | How the operator APIs verify a PingFederate access token: jwt, against PingFederate's keys, or introspection, by asking its introspection endpoint (RFC 7662) | **Per request**: Neither jwt nor introspection: every operator request is a 503 | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_OPERATOR_AUDIENCE` | Unset | The audience an operator access token must carry in aud: the value of the access token manager's audience (a JWT manager's Audience Claim Value, or an aud attribute on a reference manager) | **Per request**: Unset: every operator request is a 503, in either profile, because no token can be checked for its audience | Required in production | Yes |
| `OIDF_OPERATOR_BASE_URL` | Unset; an http or https URL | The origin operators address the operator APIs at, with no path (https://pf.example.com): a DPoP proof's htu must be this followed by the request's path, never a URL built from the Host header | **Per request**: Unset, not an origin, or http under the production profile: every operator request is a 503 | Required in production | Yes |
| `OIDF_OPERATOR_JWKS_URL` | Unset; an http or https URL | PingFederate's JWKS for the access token manager's signing keys (https://pf.example.com/pf/JWKS for the central signing key), in jwt mode | **Per request**: Unset in jwt mode: every operator request is a 503; unreachable: a 503 once the keys held are 20 minutes old | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_OPERATOR_ACCESS_TOKEN_TYP` | `at+jwt` | The typ header PingFederate's JWT access token manager puts on its tokens (its Type Header Value), in jwt mode: at+jwt or application/at+jwt as RFC 9068 asks, the default; none for a manager whose field is blank, which then requires the header to be missing; or another value, compared exactly | **Per request**: Not the manager's value: every operator request in jwt mode is a 401 invalid_token | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_OPERATOR_INTROSPECTION_ENDPOINT` | Unset; an http or https URL | PingFederate's introspection endpoint (https://pf.example.com/as/introspect.oauth2), in introspection mode | **Per request**: Unset in introspection mode: every operator request is a 503; unreachable: a 503 | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_OPERATOR_INTROSPECTION_CLIENT_ID` | Unset | The client the operator APIs introspect tokens as (client_secret_basic); it needs the Access Token Validation grant | **Per request**: Unset in introspection mode: every operator request is a 503; wrong: PingFederate answers 401 and every operator request is a 503 | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_OPERATOR_INTROSPECTION_CLIENT_SECRET` | Unset; a secret, never shown | The introspecting client's secret | **Per request**: Unset in introspection mode: every operator request is a 503; wrong: every operator request is a 503 | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_OPERATOR_INSECURE_TLS` | `false` | Trusts any certificate on the JWKS and introspection calls, through platform's InsecureTls; the host name is still checked | **Not checked**: Read strictly: true or false | Not in production: `true` | Yes |
| `OIDF_OPERATOR_AUTH_FAILURES_PER_MINUTE` | `10`; a whole number, 1 to 10000 | How many failed authentications one client address may make in a minute before every operator request from it is a 429 until the minute ends | **Per request**: Not a whole number from 1 up: every operator request is a 503 | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_OPERATOR_MUTATIONS_PER_MINUTE` | `60`; a whole number, 1 to 100000 | How many changes one operator (the token's subject) may make in a minute before the next is a 429 until the minute ends | **Per request**: Not a whole number from 1 up: every operator request is a 503 | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_OPERATOR_DPOP_NONCE` | `true` | Whether a DPoP proof to the operator APIs must carry a nonce they issued (RFC 9449 section 9): a proof without one, or with one not issued in the current minute or the one before, is a 401 use_dpop_nonce with the nonce to use in DPoP-Nonce, and a proof is then good only within the window the server chose, not the client's clock. The nonce secret is shared through Redis when OIDF_REDIS_URL is set, and is this JVM's own otherwise | **Per request**: false under the production profile: every operator request is a 503. Anything but true or false: every operator request is a 503 | Not in production: `false` | Yes |
| `OIDF_AUTHORITY_ADMIN_TOKEN` (system property `oidf.authority.admin_token`, then env `OIDF_AUTHORITY_ADMIN_TOKEN`) | Unset; a secret, never shown | The development static bearer: in the development profile, a request presenting exactly this token as Authorization: Bearer (compared in constant time) is let through any operator route - /federation/admin/*, hosted-entity enrolment and revocation, /federation/registered-clients, and (from the system property or the environment, never an init-param) /agentic-identity/health and /agentic-identity/info - beside PingFederate-issued access tokens, with a WARN per request that names the route. Production never accepts it, and while it is set every operator request is a 503 and the operator API component is REFUSED with a reason that says to remove it (Phase 3 decision 20); operators use PingFederate access tokens there (docs/operator/operator-authentication.md). On one of pf-integration's servlets the init-param adminToken (hosted-entities), when set, is used in its place | **Per request**: Set in production: every operator request is a 503 until it is removed. Wrong in development: the request goes on to the access-token check, and counts against the failed-authentication limit when that refuses it | Not in production: any value; refuses `OPERATOR_API` | Yes |
